pr.title: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain

raw_findings.body: The derived website_name (host/path) is still emitted in the serialized JSON for restricted/anonymous viewers even though the underlying website field is explicitly hidden for the same audience, leaking private profile information through a side channel.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Serializer discloses derived sensitive data to unauthorized viewers despite the source field being intentionally hidden.
raw_findings.impact: The derived website_name (host/path) is still emitted in the serialized JSON for restricted/anonymous viewers even though the underlying website field is explicitly hidden for the same audience, leaking private profile information through a side channel.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new website_name attribute was added without reusing the existing untrusted_attributes/restrict_user_fields gating that protects the underlying website field.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update include_website_name to also honor scope.restrict_user_fields?(object), e.g. `website.present? && !scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, or register :website_name via the same untrusted_attributes mechanism used for :website.
raw_findings.title: website_name attribute bypasses the TL0/anonymous privacy restriction applied to website
raw_findings.trigger: A TL0 user is viewed anonymously (restrict_user_fields? is true) and has user_profile.website set; :website is suppressed for this viewer via untrusted_attributes, but include_website_name only checks website.present?, not the same restriction.

raw_findings.body: The serialized JSON includes `website_name: null` instead of omitting the key, diverging from the established include_<attr>? convention used elsewhere in this file (e.g. include_card_image_badge_id checks the computed attribute's own presence).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent serializer behavior producing a null attribute where callers/tests may expect the key to be absent.
raw_findings.impact: The serialized JSON includes `website_name: null` instead of omitting the key, diverging from the established include_<attr>? convention used elsewhere in this file (e.g. include_card_image_badge_id checks the computed attribute's own presence).
raw_findings.root_cause: include_website_name was implemented to check the raw source field (website) instead of the attribute it gates (website_name).
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change include_website_name to check the computed value, e.g. `website_name.present?`, matching the pattern used for other computed attributes in this serializer.
raw_findings.title: include_website_name checks the wrong field's presence, allowing a null website_name in the JSON payload
raw_findings.trigger: user_profile.website is a non-empty but unparsable/host-less value (e.g. a relative path or malformed URL), so URI(website.to_s).host is nil and website_name returns nil, while website.present? is still true.

raw_findings.body: URI(website.to_s) is parsed twice per call (once at the top for .host, again in the branch for .path), doing unnecessary duplicate work on every serialization of a user record.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary repeated parsing work in a hot serialization path.
raw_findings.impact: URI(website.to_s) is parsed twice per call (once at the top for .host, again in the branch for .path), doing unnecessary duplicate work on every serialization of a user record.
raw_findings.root_cause: The method calls URI(website.to_s) independently in multiple places instead of caching the parsed result.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Parse the URI once into a local variable (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) at the top of the method and reuse uri.host/uri.path throughout.
raw_findings.title: Redundant re-parsing of the website URL in website_name
raw_findings.trigger: Any user with a website set that hits a code path returning the concatenated host+path (all three branches of website_name).

raw_findings.body: This branch (equal-length subdomain comparison) is entirely unexercised by the added specs; a regression here (e.g. off-by-one in the split/slice logic) would go undetected by the test suite.
raw_findings.evidence:
elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
      # www.example.com == forum.example.com
      website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regressions possible in an untested conditional branch of privacy/display-affecting logic.
raw_findings.impact: This branch (equal-length subdomain comparison) is entirely unexercised by the added specs; a regression here (e.g. off-by-one in the split/slice logic) would go undetected by the test suite.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new elsif branch of website_name was added without a corresponding spec assertion covering it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add spec cases for this branch, e.g. asserting website_name shows the full path when website host and discourse_host share a common parent domain with equal segment counts, and a negative case where the parent domains differ.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for the subdomain-to-subdomain website_name matching branch
raw_findings.trigger: A website host and discourse_host with the same number of domain segments and more than two segments, e.g. website 'http://www.example.com/user' vs discourse_host 'forum.example.com'.

finding.trigger: user_profile.website is a non-empty but unparsable/host-less value (e.g. a relative path or malformed URL), so URI(website.to_s).host is nil and website_name returns nil, while website.present? is still true.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that website_name:null would be emitted is incorrect. When website.present? is false, include_website_name returns false and the attribute is omitted entirely per ActiveModel::Serializer convention. When website.present? is true but URI parsing fails to extract host, website_name returns nil early (line 140), but include_website_name still returns true. However, this edge case requires a malformed URL that passes present? but has no host - a narrow scenario with minimal impact, and the claim about convention violation is unsubstantiated.
